subject: Exception request: safety cutover + automatic version pin for OmniPay A/B

Subject: Exception request: safety cutover + automatic version pin for OmniPay A/B

Hi Carlos / OmniPay ops team —

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. As OmniPay moves the payment routing experiment (A/B split) into a higher traffic window next week, the customer has asked for stronger uptime and latency guarantees during the rollout window. Their procurement team wants an explicit mitigation plan that keeps live traffic within SLA obligations if latency or error rates regress.

We'd like to request an operational exception to allow the following temporary canary policy for this account (details below) while we complete performance tuning:

- 10% A/B traffic ramp (OmniPay-B) for 48 hours.
- Automatic pin to last-known-good model version for OmniPay-B when:
  - 99th pct latency increases by >80ms sustained over 2 minutes, OR
  - error rate for generation calls >1.5% for 5 minutes.
- Immediate traffic rebalancing (shift back to OmniPay-A) if pin fails or doesn't restore baseline within 3 minutes.

This policy would be implemented as an account-scoped rollout rule with automated monitoring + an escape hatch for on-call. Can you confirm OmniPay is comfortable with this behavior? We will provide the SLA carveout doc and a short attestation for procurement.

I've attached the canary safety matrix and the proposed auto-pin snippet for the ops runbook. Marcus — can you review the thresholds and confirm the detection windows are realistic from a runtime perspective?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Kimberly —

Appreciate the summary. A couple quick clarifying Qs from our SRE and procurement folks:

1) If the auto-pin triggers, will the pinned variant still be subject to the same SLA accounting (i.e., do we need a separate service credit carveout)?
2) How will you surface the pin event to our telemetry (we need an event in our Splunk stream and a webhook to notify our incident channel)?
3) Does the pin logic require a cold restart of instances, or is this a routing-level pin that switches traffic without container restarts?

Procurement also asked for a one-page attestation that this exception is temporary and that Redwood will revert to standard rollout guardrails once tuning completes.

If you can answer these, we can sign off from our side and loop our procurement lead.

—Carlos

Subject: Re: Exception request: safety cutover + automatic version pin for OmniPay A/B

Hi Carlos / team —

Short answers up front:
1) Pin behavior & SLA accounting: The auto-pin is a routing-level override that sends OmniPay-B traffic to a pre-specified model version (last-known-good). From our backend perspective there is no model restart; requests are routed to an already-loaded variant. For billing/SLA, we recommend the exception document mark the pin as an operational mitigation — telemetry and requests still count toward usage but we will agree in writing that temporary SLA nonconformances during the canary window will be governed by a limited carveout (one-time credit if the pinned state cannot restore baseline within agreed windows).

2) Observability hooks: We will emit a structured event (json) to your webhook endpoint when the auto-pin fires, and will replicate the same event into a shared Splunk forwarder (we will need the endpoint + token). The event includes: account_id, timestamp, trigger_reason, pre/post 99p latency, error_rate.

3) Runtime behavior: This is a routing override — no container cold restarts. We maintain warm KV caches for the pinned variant; if the pinned model isn't warm we'll fall back to traffic shift back to OmniPay-A to avoid latency spikes.

Proposed refinement to thresholds (based on runtime latency distribution):
- Trigger: 99p latency +80ms sustained for 120s OR generation error rate >1.25% sustained for 300s.
- Auto-pin action: route traffic to pinned model, annotate event, send webhook, begin 3-minute stabilisation timer.
- Recovery check: if within 3 minutes pre-post metrics return to baseline, keep pin; else auto-shift traffic back to OmniPay-A and create an incident.

I've attached the operational snippets for the routing rule (auto-pin-fallback-snippets.txt) and the safety matrix PDF.

If those thresholds look sensible you can attach the short attestation and I'll ask Grace for final approval to ship the exception.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Runtime
